title: B1 · L5 — Narrative tenses combined
topic: Narrative tenses: past simple, past continuous, past perfect
description: Combinación de tiempos narrativos: past simple para eventos principales, past continuous para fondo y past perfect para acciones anteriores.

questions.prompt: Cuentas cómo te interrumpieron mientras hacías algo cotidiano.
questions.question: Complete: 'While I ___ dinner, the phone ___.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous ('was cooking') para la acción de FONDO/proceso; past simple ('rang') para la acción PUNTUAL que interrumpe. Regla mnemotécnica: la 'película larga' va en continuous, la 'foto puntual' en simple. Error típico: usar dos past simples y perder el contraste fondo/evento.
examples: While she was reading, the doorbell suddenly rang. → fondo + interrupción
While we were watching TV, the lights went out. → escena en curso + evento puntual

questions.prompt: Describes la escena que encontraste al llegar a casa.
questions.question: Complete: 'When I got home, my sister ___ dinner and my dad ___ a nap.'
questions.explanation: Dos acciones EN CURSO simultáneas en el pasado → ambas en past continuous. Es la fotografía de la escena que encontraste al llegar. Error típico: usar past simple ('cooked / took') que sugiere que ambos empezaron justo cuando llegaste, perdiendo la idea de escena en marcha.
examples: When I arrived, they were laughing and playing board games. → escena en marcha
When she called, I was cooking and listening to music. → dos acciones simultáneas

questions.statement: In a story, past perfect is used to mention something that happened earlier than the main past events.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. El past perfect ('had + participio') retrocede aún más atrás en la línea de tiempo que el past simple principal. Es como añadir una 'capa de flashback' dentro del pasado narrativo. Muy útil para explicar antecedentes o causas anteriores.
examples: I called Anna, but she had already left the office. → flashback dentro del pasado
He was upset because his team had lost the match. → causa anterior

questions.text: As we were walking home, we noticed that someone had followed us.
questions.explanation: Nota el linking suave 'as-we' y la contracción típica en habla: 'we'd been followed'. 'Had followed' se pronuncia rápido, casi 'hadfollowed'. Estructura de misterio: 'As + past continuous + past simple + past perfect' — tres tiempos en una frase de historia.
examples: As she was leaving, she realised she'd forgotten her bag. → tres tiempos combinados
As they were talking, they noticed someone had entered the room. → efecto suspense

questions.question: Choose: 'I ___ dinner when I ___ that I ___ the meat.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous (was cooking, fondo) + past simple (realised, momento clave) + past perfect (had burned, anterior al momento clave). Los tres tiempos narrativos en secuencia perfecta. Error típico: usar solo past simples y perder la profundidad temporal.
examples: I was driving when I realised I'd left my phone at home. → tres capas de tiempo
She was reading when she noticed someone had switched the light on. → misma estructura

questions.prompt: Empareja cada función narrativa con el tiempo verbal correcto:

pairs.left: Action before the main past event
Duration up to a past point

questions.explanation: Los cuatro tiempos trabajan juntos en las narraciones: past simple es el hilo principal (qué pasó); past continuous es el decorado (qué estaba pasando); past perfect es el flashback (qué había pasado antes); past perfect continuous es la duración previa (cuánto tiempo llevaba pasando).
examples: I opened the door — main event → past simple
It was pouring with rain — background → past continuous

questions.prompt: Explicas por qué tu jefe estaba destrozado esta mañana.
questions.question: Complete: 'He was exhausted because he ___ all night.'
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous ('had been working') explica un estado pasado con foco en la DURACIÓN de la causa. 'Was working' solo describiría la acción sin explicar el estado; 'has worked' es presente perfect, incorrecto en narrativa pasada.
examples: She was starving because she hadn't eaten all day. → causa negativa prolongada
They were on cloud nine because they'd been dancing for hours. → efecto positivo

questions.target: I was walking home when I bumped into an old friend I hadn't seen in years — what a coincidence.
questions.explanation: Situación: cuentas un encuentro casual sorprendente. Combina past continuous (was walking, fondo) + past simple (bumped into, evento puntual) + past perfect (hadn't seen, referencia anterior). 'What a coincidence' añade el toque emocional real de las anécdotas.
examples: I was cooking when I remembered I'd forgotten to buy salt — typical. → tres tiempos + reacción
We were driving when we noticed the sun had already set. → escena + descubrimiento

questions.statement: It is correct to use past simple for both the main story events AND their background actions.
questions.explanation: FALSO. El fondo va en past continuous para distinguirlo de los eventos puntuales que hacen avanzar la historia (past simple). Si usas past simple para todo, la narración pierde profundidad y todo suena en el mismo plano temporal.
examples: It was raining. Suddenly, the door opened. → fondo (continuous) + evento (simple)
We were chatting when someone screamed. → contraste fondo/interrupción

questions.prompt: Cuentas un mal recuerdo de un viaje.
questions.question: Which sentence best shows correct narrative tenses?
options: We arrived at the hotel and someone stole our bags.
We were arriving at the hotel when someone had stolen our bags.
When we arrived at the hotel, we realised someone had stolen our bags.
When we had arrived at the hotel, someone stole our bags.
questions.explanation: Orden correcto: 1) alguien robó las maletas (anterior, past perfect), 2) llegamos y nos dimos cuenta (posterior, past simple). Opción B usa 'arriving' con 'had stolen' de forma incoherente. Opción D invierte el orden lógico del past perfect.
examples: When I opened the fridge, I realised someone had eaten the cake. → descubrimiento + causa anterior
When she got home, she saw someone had left flowers on the doorstep. → sorpresa + acción previa

questions.text: The sun was setting when we finally reached the top of the mountain.
questions.explanation: Nota el linking 'sun-was' fluido. 'Reached' se pronuncia con /tʃ/ suave. Estructura muy vívida para descripciones de logros o momentos épicos: past continuous (was setting, decorado natural) + past simple (reached, culminación).
examples: The birds were singing when we finally opened the window. → escena + acción
The rain was falling steadily when we started our journey. → decorado + inicio

questions.prompt: Cuentas una anécdota del cine con amigos.
questions.question: Complete: 'By the time the film started, we ___ our popcorn.'
questions.explanation: 'By the time + past simple' + past perfect es una combinación fija: la acción del past perfect se completó ANTES del momento marcado. 'Had already eaten' subraya que ya no quedaba. Error típico: usar present perfect ('have already eaten') calcado del español.
examples: By the time we arrived, they'd already left — bad timing. → orden claro
By the time she called, I'd already gone to bed, obviously. → acción completada antes

questions.statement: In storytelling, we can mix past simple, past continuous and past perfect within the same paragraph.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Los tres tiempos suelen convivir en un mismo párrafo para dar orden temporal, profundidad y ritmo a las historias. De hecho, una narración natural en inglés que solo usa past simple suena plana y básica.
examples: It was raining. I was walking home when I saw a man who had lost his dog. → tres tiempos en dos frases
She was cooking. The phone rang. She realised she'd forgotten to buy oil. → mezcla natural

questions.prompt: Cuentas cómo os despertó un ruido extraño anoche.
questions.question: Choose: 'While we ___ , we suddenly ___ a loud noise.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous ('were sleeping', fondo prolongado) + past simple ('heard', evento puntual interruptor). 'Hear' es verbo de percepción — casi nunca se usa en continuous ('were hearing' sería incorrecto). 'Suddenly' encaja perfecto con acciones puntuales interruptoras.
examples: While we were sleeping, someone broke in through the back door. → fondo + irrupción
While she was studying, the fire alarm suddenly went off. → concentración + susto

questions.target: It was a rainy afternoon and I was reading when I suddenly remembered I'd left my window wide open.
questions.explanation: Situación: cuentas una anécdota doméstica en una charla casual. Frase modelo con tres tiempos: past continuous (was reading, escena), past simple (remembered, evento clave), past perfect (had left, causa anterior). 'Suddenly' y 'wide open' añaden vividez.
examples: It was late and I was working when I realised I hadn't eaten anything all day. → escena + evento + causa
It was quiet and she was reading when she noticed someone had knocked at the door. → tres capas temporales
